text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid says in a seminar in Alexandria that the country's privatisation programme has shown an improvement in the profits of the public sector companies to 50 billion pounds. He said shares in 55 companies until now have been sold off and by the end of June the number will reach 88. The sell-offs are worth some 4,800 million pounds.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa calls for national reconciliation in Somalia and welcomes Laurent Kabila. Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will visit Cairo for talks on the Middle East peace process after the Organisation of African Unity conference in Harare, Zimbabwe in the coming week.
- Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi says that he discussed during his visit to Holland the opportunities for the country to participate in exploring for oil and gas in Egypt.
- Presidential envoy Osama el-Baz will return to Israel this week to continue the efforts of Egypt to save the peace process.
- Minister of State for Economic Affairs Youssef Boutros Ghali says that more than 20 international banks have sought to invest in Egypt because of the success of privatisation.
